criteria.text: Chronic gout in adults refractory to conventional therapy.
Patient is 18 years of age or older.
Prescribed by or in consultation with a rheumatologist or nephrologist.
Chronic gout defined by at least one qualifying manifestation.
Baseline serum uric acid is at least 6 mg/dL.
Patient has been screened for G6PD deficiency.
Allopurinol: contraindication, intolerance, or treatment failure after 3 months of therapy (both drugs required).
Febuxostat: contraindication, intolerance, or treatment failure after 3 months of therapy (both drugs required).
Currently (within the last 30 days) receiving gout flare prophylaxis with NSAIDs, colchicine, or both, or contraindication to use.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Krystexxa (pegloticase), a PEGylated uric acid specific enzyme. Version 1; Original 2/17/2022; Approval 4/15/2022; Effective 6/1/2022.

Encoded: closed refractory chronic gout indication and approval criteria 1-7. Both allopurinol and febuxostat must independently qualify: contraindication, intolerance, or treatment failure after 3 months of therapy. Denial criterion is failure to meet approval criteria.

Cautions (notes only): anaphylaxis can occur with any infusion; patients should be pre-medicated and monitored. Screen patients at risk for G6PD deficiency; screening is encoded, not a negative-result requirement. Gout flare prophylaxis is recommended for at least the first 6 months of therapy. Congestive heart failure exacerbation may occur; monitor accordingly.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months if the prescriber documents positive clinical response to therapy.
Quantity (notes only): one 8 mg IV infusion every two weeks (16 mg per month, 2 vials); HCPCS J2507, maximum 16 billable units. max_units is null; quantity is not evaluated.
Documentation verification, safety monitoring, duration, reauthorization response, and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial.
